questions.enonce_markdown:
"While I am in the world, I am the light of the world" (John 9;5). Discuss this statement showing its culmination in the theme 'Spiritual Blindness'.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** In John 9:5 Jesus says, "As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world", just before he heals a man born blind. Light is a major image of the Fourth Gospel (1:4-9; 3:19-21; 8:12; 12:35-36, 46). The healing in chapter 9 shows that his coming divides people into those who see and those who refuse to see, and so the theme of light reaches its climax in the theme of spiritual blindness.

**1. The statement.**
- *Light in John.* The prologue says that "in him was life, and the life was the light of men; the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it" (1:4-5). In John 8:12 Jesus says "I am the light of the world; whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life".
- "*While I am in the world*" points to a limited time, as in 9:4 ("night is coming, when no one can work") and 12:35. The Gospel emphasises the urgency of response.
- Light reveals, guides, gives life and judges: those who come to it are known by their deeds (3:19-21).

**2. Chapter 9 as a drama of light and blindness.**
- The disciples ask whether sin caused the blindness. Jesus rejects the idea and says that the works of God are to be shown in him (9:2-3).
- He makes clay, anoints the eyes and sends the man to wash in the pool of Siloam (9:6-7), and the man sees.
- The man's physical sight is matched by growing spiritual sight. He first calls Jesus "the man called Jesus" (9:11), then "a prophet" (9:17), then says that Jesus must be "from God" (9:33), and finally says "Lord, I believe", and worships him (9:38).
- The Pharisees, who claim to see, go the other way. They investigate, question the parents, split among themselves, and accuse Jesus of being a sinner because of the Sabbath. They drive the man out (9:34).
- Jesus concludes: "For judgment I came into this world, that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind" (9:39). To the Pharisees' question "Are we also blind?" he replies "If you were blind, you would have no guilt; but now that you say 'We see', your guilt remains" (9:40-41).

**3. Culmination of the theme of spiritual blindness.**
- Spiritual blindness is not ignorance but refusal to accept the light. It appears in other places: Nicodemus who comes by night (3:2), the crowds who do not recognise the signs (6:26), and "the Jews" who reject him (12:37-40).
- Those who recognise their need receive sight, while those confident in their own knowledge are blind. The healing becomes a sign that Jesus is the one who gives light.
- Judgment in John is therefore not an external sentence but a result of how a person responds to the light.

**Conclusion.** The statement "I am the light of the world" finds its fullest illustration in the healing of the man born blind. The chapter shows that the coming of Jesus brings crisis: some come to see, others reject the light and remain in blindness. The theme invites the reader to respond in faith, as the blind man did.
